diagnostics.message: :output.custom_role_id: explicit depends_on of :resource.google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles is redundant — already implied by attribute references

google_organization_iam_binding.authoritative assigns role = each.key from input strings, so grants of custom roles created by google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles can run before those roles exist. Resolve locally managed role names through the custom-role resources, falling back to the supplied name for other roles.

google_organization_iam_member.additive takes its role from string-valued inputs without depending on google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles. If an additive grant uses a custom role created here, Terraform can attempt the grant before creating the role. Reference the managed role name when available.

google_organization_iam_policy.authoritative obtains policy_data from input-derived JSON, which does not establish an ordering dependency on google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles. When its bindings include custom roles created here, policy application must wait for those roles to exist; add a dependency on the custom-role resources.
output.custom_role_id already references google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles in its value comprehension, so its explicit depends_on on the same resources duplicates the implicit dependency.

output.id already depends on google_org_policy_policy.default, which explicitly depends on google_organization_iam_audit_config.config. The direct depends_on on the audit configuration is transitively redundant.
